title: Japan makes a fridge for humans to chill workers during extreme heat - The Star

full_text:
Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan’s punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company’s newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans.
The phonebooth-sized machine, where jets of chilled air ensure ice-cold comfort, only launched this year but has proved popular in a country that seems to be getting inexorably warmer.
“I was really able to recover thanks to that. Once you use it, it’s very, very cool,” said Isao, 51, in the western industrial city of Higashiosaka.
Tokyo-based industrial equipment distributor Trusco Nakayama said it has sold more than 300 units of the “Do Hiemon Box” since April, priced at JPY1.5mil (RM380,464).
Customers include construction sites, factories and warehouses, and will expand in the future to golf courses, said company sales agent China Yamamoto. Baseball stadiums may also be interested.
Some within the company had been sceptical, she added.
“It’s large, it’s expensive, and it’s not the kind of product where you can just explain it in words and have customers say, ‘Okay, let’s buy one’.
“So there were a lot of uncertainties,” she said.
Cruelly hot
Scientists say human-induced climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events around the world. In 2025, Japan saw its hottest summer on record.
This year, the weather office began using a new word – “kokushobi” or “cruelly hot day” – when temperatures hit 40°C, urging the public to treat extreme heat like a natural disaster.
Tokyo alone recorded almost 120 heat-related deaths in the month to mid-August, while close to 63,000 people nationwide this summer needed emergency care.
Since last year, Japanese businesses have faced tougher legal requirements to help employees toiling in the heat.
Building sites, for example, must provide workers with suitable clothing such as jackets with built-in fans, as well as air-conditioned break rooms and canopies to ensure shade.
A new initiative introduced this year allows bureaucrats in Tokyo to come to work in shorts – a groundbreaking move in a country where formal business attire still rules.
The impact of rising temperatures on businesses in the world’s fourth-biggest economy is real.
A survey in July by Teikoku Databank found that 50% of companies said intense heat had disrupted their operations.
Almost 88% said they had upgraded efforts to help workers cope with the heat.
Vital investment
The Do Hiemon Box can provide one line of defence.
It operates from a regular power socket, can be wheeled around and doesn’t use much power, according to its maker.
To prevent overuse, it automatically shuts off after 20 minutes.
Investing in heat-countering measures has become essential to maintain the existing workforce and attract new recruits, said Yutaka Kono from Konoe, the specialist wholesaler of screws and surveying equipment where Tabuchi works.
Conventional air conditioners and spot coolers offer relief, but Yutaka’s firm has many open areas to allow trucks and heavy equipment to operate.
“I was really surprised by this new concept of putting people into a kind of refrigerator, and I found it very appealing that by going inside that refrigerator, a person’s body can be cooled in an instant to a safe temperature,” said Yutaka.
“That made me think, ‘We definitely want to install one of these’,” he said.
Worker Taichi Konishi, 24, says he uses it about three times a day.
After moving heavy boxes of metal tools and parts by hand between cargo pallets, he strolls over, steps into the box, sits down and smiles, running his fingers through his hair like in the shower.
“This feels really good,” he said.
“I’ve only been in for about two minutes, but even that was enough for all my sweat to dry up.” – AFP

Trump-shaped ecstasy pills could be lethal, Netherlands institute issues red alert
The Trimbos Institute has issued a red alert over Trump-themed ecstasy pills found in the Netherlands. The warning focuses on their very high PMMA content, which can raise the risk of overdose and death.
Advertisement
The pills feature an image resembling Trump's face on one side, while the other side is stamped with the words “Trump” and “NL.” (Credits: Instagram/Trimbos Institute)
A Dutch mental health and addiction institute has issued a “red alert” warning over potentially lethal ecstasy pills designed to resemble US President Donald Trump.
The Utrecht-based Trimbos Institute said several of the pills had recently been submitted to drug-testing centres across the Netherlands, where they were found to contain a “very high” concentration of PMMA, or para-methoxymethamfetamine.
The institute urged people not to consume the pills under any circumstances, warning that PMMA can cause potentially fatal health complications.
The pills feature an image resembling Trump's face on one side, while the other side is stamped with the words “Trump” and “NL”. Photographs released by the institute showed pills with different coloured faces, including green and yellow.
PMMA CAN INCREASE OVERDOSE RISK
PMMA is chemically similar to MDMA, the main psychoactive substance in ecstasy. However, according to the Trimbos Institute, its effects can take longer to appear and may not produce the expected stimulating sensation associated with MDMA.
This delayed effect can increase the risk that users consume more of the drug, potentially resulting in an overdose.
The institute warned that people who take PMMA-containing pills could experience symptoms including nausea, an elevated heart rate, overheating, epileptic seizures and loss of consciousness. In severe cases, the substance can cause serious heart problems and death.
Trimbos Institute spokesperson Anniek Groothuis told the Associated Press that the institute was not aware of any reported deaths or serious illnesses linked to the pills. “We do not know of any victims where PMMA was found in their blood,” she said.
ECSTASY REMAINS POPULAR IN NETHERLANDS
Although producing, selling and using ecstasy is illegal in the Netherlands, the drug remains popular, particularly at clubs, festivals and other nightlife events.
A Dutch government report published in 2024 said around 550,000 people had taken ecstasy in 2022, describing it as a widely used party drug.
The Trimbos Institute operates a national drug-testing network involving 12 participating organisations and 34 testing locations across the country.
The Trump-themed pills are not the first ecstasy tablets inspired by the US president. In 2017, German police seized around 5,000 carrot-coloured ecstasy tablets shaped like Trump's head. Authorities believed they had been promoted online with the slogan, “Trump makes partying great again.”

Rainfall activity is set to intensify across Odisha as a fresh low-pressure area is likely to develop over the northwest Bay of Bengal on Saturday, August 29, under the influence of a cyclonic circulation.
The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Bhubaneswar, has issued an orange warning for six districts, forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall. A yellow warning has also been issued for 24 districts as several parts of the state may experience thunderstorms accompanied by lightning.
The weather system is expected to bring an increase in rainfall activity from August 30, with many areas likely to witness thunderstorms over the next four days.
Six districts under orange warning
According to RMC Director Manorama Mohanty, several districts are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall as the weather system develops.
Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Balasore, Bhadrak, Kendrapara and Jagatsinghpur are among the districts expected to experience intense rainfall.
“Various places across the state are likely to receive light to moderate rainfall. Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Balasore, Bhadrak, Kendrapara and Jagatsinghpur districts are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall,” Mohanty said.
The forecast comes amid heightened monsoon activity over Odisha and adjoining areas of the Bay of Bengal.
Heavy rain forecast in several other districts
Apart from the districts under the orange warning, heavy rainfall is also likely at some places in Puri, Khordha, Nayagarh, Jajpur, Angul, Dhenkanal, Sundargarh, Sambalpur, Deogarh, Bargarh, Nuapada, Bolangir, Nabarangpur, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Boudh and Sonepur.
Several areas may also experience thunderstorms and lightning during the period.
With the low-pressure area expected to become more influential from Sunday, rainfall activity could increase further across different parts of the state.
Residents advised to remain cautious
Authorities have urged people, particularly those living in districts under the orange warning, to remain alert and take necessary precautions.
Residents have also been advised to exercise caution during thunderstorms and lightning and stay updated with official weather advisories.
The developing system over the Bay of Bengal is expected to keep Odisha’s weather unsettled over the coming days, with periods of heavy rainfall likely in several districts.

Ecuador has declared a nationwide red alert to strengthen preparations and response measures for El Niño. Photo: EFE
Ecuador activates emergency committees and preventive measures as authorities warn 1.3 million people could be exposed across 17 provinces.
Ecuador’s government declared a nationwide red alert on Saturday as ocean-atmospheric conditions associated with the El Niño phenomenon evolve, triggering expanded preparations and emergency response measures across the country.
The National Secretariat for Risk Management (Secretaría Nacional de Gestión de Riesgos, SNGR, in Spanish) said the declaration is intended to strengthen preparedness and allow authorities to anticipate potential risk scenarios and activate mechanisms to protect the population.
Under the measure, provincial and municipal Emergency Operations Committees (COE) will be activated to coordinate preparedness and response efforts. Local governments have also been instructed to implement their existing action plans for El Niño.
Text Reads: The National Government is strengthening preparedness and response actions in the face of the possible occurrence of the El Niño Phenomenon.
The resolution provides for preventive evacuations, response protocols, the mobilization of resources and measures to protect people in areas that could be affected.
SNGR chief Carolina Lozano said about 1.3 million people could be exposed to the effects of El Niño across 17 provinces that had previously been under an orange alert.
The government has allocated $650 million across different state ministries and agencies for measures related to the phenomenon, Lozano said. About 70% of the funds are earmarked for prevention, while the remaining 30% will support response efforts.
Authorities have already reported initial impacts on the artisanal fishing sector, according to the SNGR. The agency said state institutions have been coordinating measures since February to address the effects of El Niño and reduce its potential impact on the population.
The SNGR said it will continue monitoring conditions and coordinating with different levels of government to strengthen preparedness and response efforts.
“Preparation is a shared responsibility, and for that reason, permanent monitoring, planning and coordination efforts remain in place to respond in a timely manner to any eventuality,” the agency said.
